workflow_metadata.title: Handbook for Use of Laboratory in Kibo
workflow_metadata.source: Handbook for Use of Laboratory in Kibo
workflow_metadata.source_document: Handbook for Use of Laboratory in Kibo
workflow_metadata.note: Official lifecycle metadata below is imported from the attached structured source. It is a planning/reference handbook, not a single executable astronaut procedure; missing experiment-specific actions remain explicit.
actors: Space agencies and Ethical Review Boards

workflow_steps.name: Understand space-experiment constraints
workflow_steps.action: Plan the experiment with microgravity, manned-facility safety, transport, crew-time, and refrigeration/freezing constraints.

workflow_steps.name: Specify experiment requirements
workflow_steps.action: Specify the experiment type, methods, procedures, and rationale.

workflow_steps.name: Define experiment resources
workflow_steps.action: Determine launch and collection weight, astronaut work period, power, heat, communication, and refrigeration/freezing requirements.

workflow_steps.name: Evaluate scientific and mounting feasibility
workflow_steps.action: Conduct scientific and technical/mounting-feasibility evaluation, identify risk factors, and suggest improvements.

workflow_steps.name: Return feasibility evaluation results
workflow_steps.action: Return mounting-feasibility results, technical problems, and suggested improvement measures.

workflow_steps.name: Solve identified preparation-stage problems
workflow_steps.actor: Selected researchers / proposing party with JAXA cooperation
workflow_steps.action: Work on solving identified problems during space-experiment preparation.

workflow_steps.name: Design, test and verify safety
workflow_steps.actor: JAXA mainly; proposing party when alternatives are needed
workflow_steps.action: Identify hazards, specify controls and verification, perform required design/testing, and complete safety examination.

workflow_steps.name: Develop alternative ideas when safety cannot be ensured
workflow_steps.action: Provide alternative ideas when sample or reagent safety cannot be ensured.

workflow_steps.name: Prepare life-science samples for planned launch
workflow_steps.action: Prepare and procure biological samples for the planned launch date.

workflow_steps.name: Prepare backup life-science samples
workflow_steps.action: Prepare backup samples at the launch location when short-lived biological samples could be affected by launch delay.
workflow_steps.condition: Biological sample has a short life

workflow_steps.name: Prepare life-science sample/device set and information
workflow_steps.action: Provide sample and device information, prepare sufficient on-orbit and control quantities, and ensure equipment compatibility.

workflow_steps.name: Use JAXA-provided experiment system
workflow_steps.action: Keep the experiment within the checked function/performance range of the JAXA-provided system and do not modify it in principle.
workflow_steps.condition: Experiment uses a JAXA experiment system in Table 1.4

workflow_steps.name: Develop and verify proposing-party experiment system
workflow_steps.action: Describe, design, manufacture, test, and function-verify a proposing-party system, including microgravity operation.
workflow_steps.condition: Experiment uses proposing-party tools or systems

workflow_steps.name: Provide reagent/tool information and enforce liquid/sharp-edge controls
workflow_steps.action: Provide reagent and tool information, pass safety evaluation, contain hazards, prevent liquid leakage, and avoid sharp-edged tools in principle.

workflow_steps.name: Load life-science materials using spacecraft-specific constraints
workflow_steps.action: Load according to spacecraft-specific windows, storage environments, transport capacity, and environmental restrictions.

workflow_steps.name: Execute life-science pre-start sequence
workflow_steps.actor: Launch personnel / transport system / ISS crew
workflow_steps.action: Final preparation on Earth → handover → spacecraft loading → transport to ISS → experiment-system setup on ISS.

workflow_steps.name: Wait until life-science experiment can start
workflow_steps.action: Observe the stated restriction of at least 5 days after launch before experiment start.

workflow_steps.name: Execute life-science on-orbit experiment
workflow_steps.action: Execute the specified experiment procedure, timing, devices, and tolerable operating range.

workflow_steps.name: Monitor life-science experiment
workflow_steps.actor: Ground / earth operators and Kibo experiment system
workflow_steps.action: Downlink important status and operating information when possible; distinguish real-time from recorded data.

workflow_steps.name: Store and collect life-science samples
workflow_steps.actor: ISS / Kibo operations; recovery / ground facilities
workflow_steps.action: Store samples on orbit and arrange collection/return within return-mass and recovery constraints.

workflow_steps.name: Obtain space-medicine subject approval and consent
workflow_steps.actor: Space agencies / Ethical Review Boards / experiment team
workflow_steps.action: Obtain required approvals and explain the experiment to candidate crew before obtaining consent.

workflow_steps.name: Plan baseline data collection and launch timing
workflow_steps.action: Plan baseline and ground data acquisition around launch, pre-launch crew movement, and possible post-return system needs.

workflow_steps.name: Define subjects, intervention conditions and measurements
workflow_steps.action: Specify operators, subject requirements, interventions, measurements, apparatus, experiment timing, and crew restrictions.

workflow_steps.name: Use or develop space-medicine experiment equipment
workflow_steps.action: Use checked JAXA capability or develop, test, verify, and safety-re-evaluate proposing-party equipment for space use.

workflow_steps.name: Provide space-medicine reagent/tool information and controls
workflow_steps.action: Provide material information, pass safety evaluation, control liquids and hazards, and establish special conditions for sharp instruments.

workflow_steps.name: Wait for space-medicine experiment start window
workflow_steps.action: Observe the approximately one-week post-launch restriction and restrictions during the first few weeks.

workflow_steps.name: Execute and monitor space-medicine on-orbit experiment
workflow_steps.actor: Astronaut / test subject; experiment operators; ground team
workflow_steps.action: Execute defined procedures and monitor available data, respecting uplink and data restrictions.

workflow_steps.name: Conduct post-return space-medicine experiments
workflow_steps.action: Conduct post-return experiments at Johnson Space Center within the stated day-of-return and first-10-days restrictions.

workflow_steps.name: Prepare material/physical-science samples
workflow_steps.action: Plan sample species and quantity within equipment restrictions and ensure equipment compatibility.

workflow_steps.name: Use or develop material/physical-science experiment system
workflow_steps.action: Use checked JAXA capability or describe, develop, test, and verify a proposing-party system for microgravity.

workflow_steps.name: Provide material-science reagent/tool information and controls
workflow_steps.action: Provide material information, pass safety evaluation, contain hazards, prevent liquid leakage, and avoid sharp-edged tools in principle.

workflow_steps.name: Transport and load material-science samples
workflow_steps.action: Transport materials to Johnson Space Center and stay within spacecraft storage and environmental restrictions.

workflow_steps.name: Execute material-science pre-start sequence
workflow_steps.actor: Launch personnel / transport system / ISS crew
workflow_steps.action: Final preparation on Earth → handover → spacecraft loading → transport to ISS → experiment-system setup on ISS.

workflow_steps.name: Wait until material-science experiment can start
workflow_steps.action: The source contains both at least 35 days and at least 5 days after launch; this conflict is preserved as unclear.

workflow_steps.name: Execute material-science on-orbit experiment
workflow_steps.action: Execute defined operations with specified devices, timing, tolerable range, and repeated-operation intervals.

workflow_steps.name: Monitor and manage material-science experiment
workflow_steps.actor: Ground / earth operators and Kibo experiment system
workflow_steps.action: Downlink important data when possible and account for restrictions on procedure or timing changes through uplink.

workflow_steps.name: Store and collect material-science samples
workflow_steps.actor: ISS / Kibo operations; recovery / ground facilities
workflow_steps.action: Store, collect, return, and hand over material-science samples within the stated transport and recovery limitations.

workflow_loops.condition: On-orbit monitoring permits and indicates a life-science procedure change.

workflow_parallel_processes.name: CBEF parallel-experiment capability
workflow_parallel_processes.description: CBEF microgravity and artificial-gravity compartments can support parallel experiments, but the source does not specify branch synchronization or a join condition.

missing_information: Actual experiment-specific on-orbit operation steps from start to completion are not supplied.
Exact acceptance/rejection workflow after safety or feasibility feedback is not fully specified.
Exact synchronization logic for CBEF parallel experiments is not specified.
ambiguous_information: The handbook is a planning/reference handbook rather than a single executable procedure.
Some tables state constraints and requirements rather than explicit transitions.
Space-medicine equipment-source alternatives do not have separate downstream sequences.
contradictions: Material and Physical Science contains both at least 35 days and at least 5 days after launch as the start restriction; this remains UNCLEAR_FROM_SOURCE.
